title: From Power Plant to Power Outlet

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.text: Voltage is the difference in electrical energy between two points in a circuit. It is measured in volts (V).
hint.sound: Voltage is the difference in electrical energy between two points in a circuit. It is measured in volts.

atoms.text: At the power plant, transformers “step up”, or increase, the voltage so that electricity can be transmitted efficiently across the country. Electricity is transmitted across the countryside along high-voltage power lines.
atoms.sound: ssml: At the power plant, transformers step up, or increase, the voltage so that electricity can be transmitted efficiently across the country. Electricity is transmitted across the countryside along high-voltage power lines.

atoms.a: What is electricity transmitted across the country along?

atoms.text:
The electricity travels to a substation, where transformers “step down” the voltage. Further down the line, the voltage is lowered again to make it safe to use in houses and other buildings.

Finally, electricity is supplied to houses, schools and offices via underground or overground cables.
atoms.sound: The electricity travels to a substation, where transformers step down the voltage. Further down the line, the voltage is lowered again to make it safe to use in houses and other buildings. Finally, electricity is supplied to houses, schools and offices via underground or overground cables.

atoms.a: What happens to the electricity at a substation?

instruction.text: Listen carefully and find the right picture for each step.

atoms.a: Electricity is generated at a power plant, for example a hydroelectric dam.
The voltage is “stepped up”, and electricity is transmitted across the country along high-voltage power lines.
atoms.sound: The voltage is stepped up, and electricity is transmitted across the country along high-voltage power lines.

atoms.a: The voltage is “stepped down” at a substation.
atoms.sound: The voltage is stepped down at a substation.

atoms.a: Electricity is distributed to households, and people can use their computers and fridges!
